plot: On the morning of Bird's big Morning Song in the park she gets the hiccups; Max's count-to-ten, Mouse's BOO and Dog's silly ball face all fail, until Dog, who gets nervous hiccups himself, teaches the slow 'smell the flower, blow the dandelion' breath, Bird sings beautifully, and Max ends up with the hiccups.

beats.say: HIC! Oh no! HIC! Good morning, everybody! HIC! Oh dear, not again!
It is a bright, sunny morning in the park. And today is a very big day for Bird.
Bird, today is your Morning Song! The whole park is waiting to hear you sing.
I know, Max! I practiced all week long. Listen to this. La la la... HIC!
Every hiccup pops Bird right up into the air, like a little blue popcorn.
Wow! That hiccup was bigger than me!
Is it a new dance? Can I do it too? Hic! Hic!
It is not a dance, Dog. HIC! I cannot sing a song with hiccups in the middle!
Don't worry, Bird. I know a trick. Take a big breath and hold it while I count to ten.
Bird takes a huge breath. Her cheeks puff up like two round balloons.
One... two... three... four... five... six... seven...
HIC!
Pop! Bird flies up, spins around three times, and lands upside down in the soft grass.
Seven is not ten, Max. HIC! Your trick did not work.
My turn! My grandpa says a big surprise scares hiccups away. Close your eyes, Bird.
Mouse tiptoes quietly behind Bird, up on her tiny pink toes.
BOO!
Oh, hello, Mouse! What a nice surprise to see you. HIC!
You were not even a little bit scared?
You are much too sweet to be scary, Mouse. HIC!
My turn! Silly faces always work. Look at me, Bird. Look at my super silly face!
Dog puts the red ball on his nose and crosses his eyes.
Ha ha ha! Dog, that is the silliest face in the whole wide world!
It is very funny. HIC! But my hiccups think so too. HIC! HIC!
The ball rolls off Dog's nose. Boing, boing, boing.
Three tricks and three more hiccups. What else can we try?
Maybe I should not sing today. HIC! Everybody will laugh at my hiccup song.
Bird sits down on a rock. Her feathers droop. Even her hiccups sound a little sad.
Bird? Can I ask you something? Do your wings feel all wobbly inside?
Yes! Wobbly and jumpy, like a hundred butterflies. HIC! How did you know that?
Because I get them too. When the mailman comes, my tummy gets nervous, and then... hic!
Dog! You get nervous hiccups too? I never knew that about you!
Yep. And I know the trick. It is a doggy trick. Smell the flower, then blow the dandelion.
Smell the flower? Blow the dandelion? Dog, what does that mean?
Watch me. First, a slow sniff in through your nose, like smelling a big pink flower.
Dog sniffs in slowly. Very, very slowly. His nose wiggles. His tail stays still.
Then a slow blow out, like blowing a fluffy dandelion. Whoooo. All the seeds fly away.
Smell the flower... HIC... blow the dandelion. Whoooo. Like this?
Slower, Bird. We will all do it with you. Everybody, together now!
Max, Dog, Mouse and Bird all sniff in slowly, and all blow out slowly. Once. Twice. Three times.
The park is very quiet. Everybody waits.
Wait. Listen. Do you hear that? Nothing! No hiccups at all!
Not one single hic! Dog, you are a genius!
I am? Wow. Do geniuses get an extra cookie after lunch?
Dog, you were the smartest friend today. You knew the hiccups came from feeling nervous.
Now my wings feel calm and happy. I am ready. Is the whole park still listening?
Bird flies up high onto the tallest branch. Everybody in the park looks up.
La la la, good morning, sun! Good morning, trees! Good morning to my friends below!
It is the most beautiful Morning Song the park has ever heard.
Bravo, Bird! Bravo! That was the best song in the whole... HIC!
Oh no! Now I have the hiccups! HIC! Somebody help me! What do I do?
Easy, Max. Smell the flower. Blow the dandelion. Nice and slow.
And so Max learns the doggy trick too. When your tummy feels wobbly, slow breaths help you feel calm.
Tomorrow I will sing my own Morning Song. HIC! Maybe after lunch. HIC!
